say_a.message: A woman in oilskins comes up the tunnel, looks you over without breaking stride, and says, "Run's clear to the crossing." She is not talking to you.

say_b.message: She stops, whistles two falling notes into the dark ahead, waits for two to come back, and walks on.

chitchat: "Keep to the middle of the run. The edges are where things wait."
"You want to be somewhere with a door on it before the water comes up."
"There's nothing down this way. That's deliberate."
description: A rangy woman in oilskins with a lever-action carbine slung muzzle-down and a hooded lantern hanging off her belt, unlit. She moves through the tunnels the way other people move through their own kitchen, and she has clocked you a good deal earlier than you clocked her.

bye.text: She nods once and carries on up the tunnel, and the dark takes her a lot faster than it should.

clean.text:
Something almost like approval crosses her face.

"Noticed that, did you." She adjusts the sling. "Things that breed down here breed toward the warm. Somebody decided a while back that they were not going to breed toward this particular warm."

She starts walking.

"That is all you get from me tonight."

options.label: Some of them drink for it on purpose.

earned.text:
"Everything I can do down here, I can do because I did it ten thousand times in the dark and was bad at it for four years first."

She says it without any pride in it, which is somehow worse.

"A man works nine years on a hot floor and comes out with something he did not have going in. He stood where he was put and it got into him."

"He did not do anything. It was done to him."

options.label: So a mutant and a chromed man are the same to you.

earned_bought.text:
"Same thing with a receipt."

She checks the tunnel behind you while she talks, and does not stop doing it.

"A chromed man can do what I can do and he did not do a day of the work. He went to a counter. There is nothing in him that he made."

"The Watch will not seat him and I would not want him at my back. Halcyon would fit him and warranty him. They are welcome to."

options.label: You have watched it done, then.

earned_chosen.text:
"Out south. They queue for it."

Her voice does not change, and it is the only subject tonight where she does not check the tunnel while she talks.

"The hot-floor man had it done to him. I have got no time for him and I have got nothing against him either. He was somewhere and it happened."

"The ones who drink for it stood in front of a flask, with a whole body already, and decided against it. That is not bad luck. That is a person looking at what they were and saying no thank you."

options.label: You have watched it done, then.

earned_chosen_business.text:
"It is, right up until they come north."

She starts moving again.

"And I will tell you the part that actually sticks. Every one of them had the thing I have got. A body nobody had been at. They could have kept it and they could have learned to use it, and it takes years and it is dull and it hurts."

"They found a shorter way. So no, I will not have one of them at a table with me, and I have never once been talked out of that and I have been talked at about it a great deal."

earned_chosen_hard.text:
"No, it is not."

She lets that sit longer than she has let anything sit tonight.

"I have got eleven years down here and a rifle and a way of standing that has kept me alive, and if a swallow of something out of a flask makes all of that a hobby, then I have wasted my life and so has everybody I have buried."

"So it does not. That is where I have put it and I am not moving it."

options.label: Then what do you do about the ones down here?

earned_fault.text:
"No."

She does not soften it and she does not look away.

"It is not his fault. It is also not something he did."

"Both of those are true, and neither of them makes him a man I owe anything to."

options.label: Then what do you do about the ones down here?

earned_same.text:
"One paid and one did not. Neither of them owns what they have got."

She looks at you properly for the first time in a while.

"We are the last people in this city who own our own bodies. Nothing bought, nothing put there by the ground."

"There are not many of us. There are fewer every year."

quiet_accept.text: "Across the back of the head, and walk away, and let him wake up cold and confused and alive."

quiet_offer.text:
"There is a man on Foundry Way counting doorways." Teague says it flatly. "Municipal. Damp. Harmless as a person and not harmless as a ledger, because in six weeks somebody upstairs will have a list of every door in the quarter that opens."

"Stop the counting. Leave the counter."

Her eyes come up.

"I want to be understood on the second half. We do not leave bodies. Not because we are gentle. Because a body is a reason for somebody to come and look, and looking is the only thing that has ever hurt us."

quiet_report.text: "And he is breathing." She does not make you say it twice. "Good. In a month he will tell it as the night he got mugged on Foundry Way, which is a story nobody investigates."

root.first: She has been standing in the dark long enough to have watched you arrive. When she finally speaks it is from somewhere off to your left. "Middle of the tunnel," she says. "Nothing good stands where you are standing." She steps into your light: oilskins, carbine, no particular hurry.

options.label: What are you doing down here?
Is there a line, or is it just anybody changed?
Why do you do this every night?
What do you make of the ones who drink for it?
Who else is living down here?
How do you decide what is worth putting down?
Why is this stretch so clean?
They said you could teach me.
They say there is a town of them, south.

root.text:
She stops a comfortable distance off, carbine still slung, and looks at you with the patience of somebody who has all night.

"You are a long way in," she says. "Most people do not get this deep and stay this healthy."

"Anybody come down behind you?"

south.text:
She does not answer straight away.

"Eleven years I have been down here. In that time I have put down a bit over four hundred things that used to be something else, and not once have I had to stop and work out which was which. You know on sight. That is the whole of my expertise and it has never been wrong."

She adjusts the sling.

"So somebody tells me there is a town of them out past the Curtain. Wall round it. A gate. Children in it, they say."

A beat.

"What I hear is a nest that has learned to keep house."

"I know how that sounds. Rennick has explained it to me at length, twice. He is a better man than I am and I still think he is wrong."

She starts walking.

"Go south if you like. They all come back telling me I have it wrong. Not one of them has ever told me what I was supposed to have done with the four hundred."

south_children.text:
"They do." She does not slow down. "So did the block on Ferrier Street, and I went in there too."

The lantern on her belt is still unlit. She has not needed it once.

"You want me to say the word that makes it all right. I have not got one. I have got a tunnel and a rifle and eleven years, and none of the three has ever asked me for a reason."

stance_approve.text:
She grunts. It is the closest thing to warmth she has produced all night.

"It is. And I have not met four people who will say so down here, and two of them are dead."

She unhooks the lantern off her belt and hands it to you, still unlit.

"You will not need it. Carry it anyway. If it is in your hand you will not reach for a light when something moves, and reaching for a light is how the last one went."

options.label: You could just let them stay.

stance_object.text:
"It might be."

She does not argue and she does not get angry, and that is the whole difficulty with her.

"I have got a tunnel and a rifle and eleven years. You have got a better argument than I have and it does not reach down here."

"Bring it back when you have walked this stretch a hundred times and I will listen to it properly. That is not me being clever. That is the actual offer."

options.label: I have not made my mind up.

stance_quiet.text:
She waits three seconds for you to say something, and you do not.

"Right."

She starts walking, and the distance she leaves between you is a little wider than it was coming in.

"Down here I need to know what a person does before they do it. You have just told me you are somebody I would have to guess about."

stance_quiet_undecided.text:
"Make it up on the surface."

She checks the tunnel behind you again.

"I am not asking you to agree with me. I am asking whether you would stand there while I did it. Those are different questions and only the second one is any of my business."

stance_recover.text:
It is easier to say than you expected, and she takes it at face value, which is worse.

"Good. That is all I needed."

She adjusts the sling and carries on up the tunnel.

"Come down on a Thursday. I will show you the stretch properly and you will see why it is worth keeping."

teach.text:
Teague looks at you for long enough that the lantern on her belt stops swinging.

"Somebody sent you all the way down here, so somebody thinks you are worth the walk."

She unslings the carbine and leans it against the wall, muzzle down.

"Moving. Pain. Keeping your head. Fighting, when it comes to that, and it does."

teague_backdown.text:
She turns back to the tunnel and the shape of her goes easy again.

"Right."

You walk. She does not bring it up again and she does not sulk about it, and about ten minutes later she points out a grating you would have walked into.

"Mind that. It comes up on you."

teague_left.text:
"No."

She says it without heat, and then she is walking, and she does not look back or say goodnight or tell you which way is out.

The lantern on her belt is still unlit. She has not needed it once all night and she does not need it now, and the dark takes her a great deal faster than it should.

Somewhere east of you water is moving. It takes about a minute for the sound of her boots to go, and then you are standing in a tunnel you do not know, and the last thing she gave you was the truth.

options.label: You have decided they are worth less than you.

teague_press.text:
"I could."

She stops again. The second time tonight.

"And the first winter one of them lights a fire, and the second winter there are forty of them, and the third winter I am standing in the Blind watching Halcyon walk down that tunnel with dogs, and everybody I have ever eaten with is in a van."

"I have run it. I run it most nights."

options.label: Say it again. Out loud. All of it.

teague_warning.text:
The lantern stops swinging.

She has kept her body angled to the tunnel the whole time you have been talking, watching past you, and now she turns and looks straight at you instead, which is the first careless thing she has done.

"I have. Out loud, to your face, and I am not going to take it back to make this easier."

"Now I am going to say the next part once. I am going up this tunnel in a minute. You can come, or you can keep going at me and I will go on my own, and you will be down here without a light and without me."

options.label: He is still the same man.

the_flask.text:
"I have watched it done."

She says it the way she names any other job she has been on.

"A man at the Pool with his sleeves up and his arms out, and somebody tips a flask into him, and everybody there is pleased for him. Fortnight later there is something walking about wearing his face and his voice and getting on with its day."

Her mouth does the thing a mouth does around a bad smell, and she puts it away again immediately, because she does not think it is a respectable way to argue.

the_flask_cleansed.text:
"There is. That is the part people leave out when they tell this back to me."

"The Exodus can take it out of somebody. It costs everything a person has and it hurts for about a year and some of them do not live through it, and afterwards they are just tired and ordinary and thirty."

"Come back cleansed and I will sit down and eat with you and never mention it again. That is not me being generous. That is the rule, it is written where anybody can read it, and it has not moved in forty years."

the_flask_desecration.text:
"I would not use a word like that out loud. Rennick would have a field day."

She adjusts the sling.

"But yes. There is nothing else it is."

options.label: So there is no way back for him.
You are describing a person as an infection.

the_flask_diseased.text:
"No."

It is the flattest thing she has said tonight.

"He is diseased flesh that agreed to it. There is a difference between a man with an illness and a man who went and got one on purpose, and the difference is the whole of my opinion about him."

"I do not want it near me, I do not want it near the people I eat with, and I would not have it in a room where somebody is sleeping."

options.label: You have just described putting people in the sea.

the_flask_kept_out.text:
"Until then they stay out."

She lists it like a rota, because to her it is one.

"Not the city. Not inside the wall, not on the Row, not on a tram. And not down here either — not this stretch, not the Under, not one yard of it."

"People tell me the Under is nobody's. It is ours. It is ours because we walk it every night in the dark and nobody else will, and that is how a place becomes somebody's."

the_flask_sacred.text:
"It was. That is my whole point and you have said it for me."

She stops, and she is not performing this.

"Everything else in this city belongs to somebody. The wires are read. The water is metered. A chromed man rents his own arm off a company and it goes back to them when he dies, and that is in the paperwork."

"Your body is the last thing nobody has been inside. Nobody. Not Halcyon, not the Architect, not a surgeon. End to end, it is yours, and it is the only thing left that is."

"And they open their mouths and pour something in and let it eat that."

options.label: You could walk it and find out.

the_flask_sea.text:
She takes that one properly. It is the first thing tonight she has had to think about.

"East is four miles of tunnel and a lot of it is dry."

A pause, and she does not fill it with anything.

"I have not walked all of it. I have told you that already and I am not going to pretend otherwise now because you have found a way of putting it that stings."

options.label: What is the difference between marked and turned?
You have a ladder for how much of a person somebody is.

the_grades.text:
"There are grades to it. Nobody has written them down and everybody knows them."

She counts them off without hesitating, which tells you how often this comes up.

"Clean is nothing in you and nothing done to you. That is a seat at any table we have got."

"Marked is something small that does not show. Half the Row has something. A man with a bad chest and grey patches on him is a man with a bad chest."

"Turned is when it shows. Bought is chrome. And then there is the flask."

the_grades_found.text:
She takes a while over that one.

"Then it would be in front of me and I would have to do something about it, and I would, and I would be sick about it for a month."

She starts walking again.

"Which is exactly why I do not go looking. I am not proud of that one. It is the only part of any of this I am not proud of."

the_grades_honest.text:
"Yes."

No hesitation at all. She has been here before and she got here on her own.

"There will be two people behind that door tonight with something they have not told anybody, and I have thought about which two, and then I stopped thinking about it. I am not going to go looking and I am not going to ask."

"You can call that whatever you like. I have called it a few things myself, walking."

options.label: So you tolerate exactly what you can avoid seeing.

the_grades_line.text:
"Whether you can look at them without noticing."

She says it plainly and does not appear to hear how it sounds.

"That is not me being shallow. A man nobody looks at twice brings nobody down this tunnel. A man people cross the road to stare at gets that road watched, and we are at the end of that road."

options.label: They are not doing anything to you.

the_quiet_ones.text:
"Depends what they are."

She stops walking, which she has not done since you met her.

"The ones that have gone all the way, I put down and I have told you the number. But most of what is down here is not that. Most of it is people. Families, some of them. They are down here because there is nowhere up there that will have them, and because the ground past the wall would give their children the same thing they have got."

"Those we move on."

options.label: So they walk east until they run out of tunnel.

the_quiet_ones_after.text:
"After that they are east."

She says it the way she would give you a direction, and then, because you are still standing there, she gives you the rest of it.

"The system runs a long way. Past our stretch, past the Blind, and it keeps going under the Curtain, because the Curtain is a surface problem and nobody ever built it downward."

"Four miles or so beyond that, and then it lets out into the bay."

options.label: Nobody has ever asked because nobody wants the answer.

the_quiet_ones_bay.text:
"Some of them stop before that. There are dry stretches."

She does not pretend the sentence is stronger than it is, and she does not add anything to it.

"I have been doing this eleven years and nobody has ever asked me where east goes. Not once, and I have walked a lot of people through here."

options.label: That is the argument for anything.

the_quiet_ones_harm.text:
"They are not, no."

She agrees with it flatly and it costs her nothing.

"And in a month there are forty of them and a fire and a smell of cooking, and somebody up top notices that a dead stretch of drain has got a chimney, and then Halcyon come down here with lights and dogs and they find our door instead."

"So they go east. Cold, and inconvenienced, and alive, and none of that is nothing."

options.label: So they walk east until they run out of tunnel.

the_quiet_ones_map.text:
"Some of it."

She taps the pocket the map lives in without taking it out.

"Ours stops about a mile past the last door we use. After that it is other people's drawings and most of those disagree with each other."

"I have been as far as the sump under Meltwater. It gets colder and it gets wider and the water is going the same way you are."

the_quiet_ones_where.text:
"Out of the stretch."

It is a complete answer as far as she is concerned, and she starts walking again.

"East, mostly. There is a lot of tunnel east."

options.label: Nobody has ever thanked you for it.

why_the_walk.text:
"Because somebody has to and I am good at it."

She does not dress it up and she does not look for a reaction.

"A mile back down this tunnel there is a door. Forty of us live behind it. The oldest is eighty-one. Two of them are children, and I said children should not be down here, and I was outvoted, and they are still here."

"If anybody comes down this tunnel at night, there is me, and then there is that door."

"Nobody pays me for it. I walk it again tomorrow and the night after. One night I will not come back, and one of the other four will take the round."

why_the_walk_life.text:
"It is the one I have got and I am not sorry about it."

She checks the tunnel behind you, which she has done every ninety seconds since you met her, and will keep doing after you have gone.

"The Architect sees the whole city. Every wire, every meter, every face on every street. It does not see this tunnel."

"That is five of us. Walking."

why_the_walk_thanks.text:
"No."

She sounds faintly surprised anybody would expect it.

"Pike has sat that post ten thousand times and nobody has thanked him either. That is not a complaint. If it needed thanking to get done it would not get done, and then there would be nothing down here but Halcyon."

work.text: "Walking," she says. "Same as you." A beat. "Difference is I'll be walking it again tomorrow, and the day after."

clothing_layers: a long waxed-canvas coat, black with damp at the hem
a jumper darned at both elbows
wading boots turned down below the knee

name: Teague
